passage: I'm Nilesh, and I don't like it when Tarun comes to lunch. He picks his nose and then his fingers go into his tiffin. Yesterday I wrinkled my nose and said, "Yuck, stop it!" and everyone laughed. Then Tarun said, "I don't want to sit here anymore," and moved away. I felt bad. My nose wrinkle was about the nose-picking, but it hurt him like it was about him. Tarun is sometimes alone at break. Today I told him quietly, "It's fine to sit here, but can you wash your hands first?" He nodded. I still find it gross, but I can be nice about it.

qa.q: What did Nilesh say when Tarun picked his nose at lunch?
What did Nilesh feel after Tarun moved away, and why?
qa.a: Nilesh felt bad, because the disgust at the habit hurt Tarun as a person. Nilesh realised the yuck was meant for the habit, but Tarun took it personally.

qa.q: What could Nilesh do next time something a friend does feels disgusting?
qa.a: Nilesh can speak privately and kindly about the habit, like asking Tarun to wash first, without making Tarun feel unwelcome.

qa.q: How does Tarun likely experience being laughed at?
qa.a: Tarun probably felt embarrassed and rejected in front of everyone, so he moved away.

grounding: A child wrinkles their nose and says yuck, and learns disgust aimed at a person becomes exclusion, so kindness must be taught.

passage: Teacher's note, Class 4. At lunch today Darshan said "Yuck!" loudly about Madhav's fish curry and wrinkled his nose. Other children copied him and Madhav closed his lunchbox with a small face. I asked Darshan to step out with me and asked what he noticed about the smell. He said it was strong. I said that food he isn't used to can smell strange, but that our words can make someone feel unwelcome. Darshan looked at the floor and said he did not mean Madhav. I suggested that he tell Madhav so, and he did, adding, "Can I try a little?" Madhav nodded. I will watch how the two get on at lunch.

qa.q: What food did Madhav have at lunch?
What might Darshan have been feeling when he said he did not mean Madhav, and what else could it show?
qa.a: He may have felt guilty and embarrassed once he realised the yuck hurt Madhav. It could also show he was reacting to the smell without thinking of the person.

qa.q: What could the teacher do to build kindness in the class after this?
qa.a: The teacher could talk about respecting different foods and encourage children to say "I'm not used to that" instead of "yuck".

qa.q: How might Madhav feel after Darshan asks to try a little?
qa.a: Madhav might feel relieved and included, since he nodded, though he might also still feel a little hurt from earlier.

grounding: A child says yuck at a smell; disgust aimed at a person becomes exclusion, so a teacher helps teach kindness.
